analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. Per the file_changes patch, head lines 76-87 add a 'Provider authorization guidance' section. It documents running ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests with `swift test --skip-build --no-parallel` from provider-swift/. The section says the tests use fixed snapshots and injected process identity, and that they do not run host probes, change profiles or establish native App Attest acceptance. The two supplied units are base text, start lines 1843-2535, and are unchanged surrounding documentation (Qwen/GPT-OSS/MiMo batch checks, prefix cache tenant partition checks, SSD prefix record encoding, and similar). I reviewed them against the threat model, including TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-057, T-041 and the TB-007 prefix-cache material. The added text changes no code, configuration, endpoint or authorization behavior, and it carries no secrets or injected instructions. The documented claim that a late but unexpired serving lease stays visible while removal advice requires a matching fresh decision matches the receipt/authorization alignment described in the canonical context. It does not weaken any control. It explicitly disclaims native App Attest acceptance, so it makes no overclaim against T-056 or T-054. I found no security regression and no required threat-model update. A remaining integration question is whether ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests and the status/doctor freshness code match this description. That code is outside the supplied evidence and has not been verified; it is a documentation-accuracy matter, not a vulnerability.
